column3: “Trust” is rendered “feel secure,” and “the distinguished” “the distinguished men”; “they will come to them” is rendered “To whom … comes.”
“Hamath-Rabbah” is rendered “Hamath the great,” and “good” “better”; NASB adds “Then.”
“A day evil” is rendered “the day of calamity”; NASB renders the second line as a question.
“On the mouth of the lyre” is rendered “to the sound of the harp,” and “instruments of song” “songs.”
“In bowls of wine” is rendered “wine from sacrificial bowls,” “smear” “anoint themselves,” and “sickened” “grieved”; NASB adds “While.”
“Self” is rendered “Himself,” “pride” “arrogance,” and “what fills it” “all it contains”; NASB adds “Therefore.”
“His loved one” is rendered “one’s uncle,” and “the one who burns him” “his undertaker”; “not to bring to remembrance” is rendered “not to be mentioned.”
“Someone will strike” is rendered “be smashed,” and “rubbles” “fragments.”
“Plow with oxen” is rendered “plow them with oxen”; the Hebrew may be divided “plow the sea with oxen,” so the meaning is uncertain.
“Oppress” is rendered “afflict,” “Lebo Hamath” “the entrance of Hamath,” and “wadi” “brook.”
